blocks.title: Molar concentration
blocks.text: The molar concentration of a solution, in mol/dm3, is the number of moles of a substance (reactant or product) dissolved per volume of solution in dm3: C = n / V, so n = C x V.

Here C is the molar concentration and V the volume of the solution. Molar concentration completes the set of routes to the mole: mass over molar mass, volume over molar volume, particles over Avogadro's number, and concentration times volume. Sample Problem 4.10: 27.64 g of K2CO3 dissolved in 1 dm3 of solution; the molar mass of K2CO3 is 138.2 g/mol, so n = 27.64 / 138.2 = 0.2 mol and C = 0.2 mol / 1 dm3 = 0.2 mol/dm3.

blocks.caption: Routes to the number of moles

blocks.prompt: Calculate the molar concentration of 7.9 g of KMnO4 (molar mass 158 g/mol) dissolved in 1 dm3 of solution, and of 4.0 g of NaOH (40 g/mol) in 250 cm3.

items: Molar concentration C = n / V in mol/dm3, and n = C x V; 27.64 g of K2CO3 (138.2 g/mol) in 1 dm3 is 0.2 mol/dm3.
